rv.q: And that is exactly the feeling Birbiglia gives us at 'The New One.'

On those terms, Mike Birbiglia‘s "The New One," transferred from a sold-out downtown engagement to a limited Broadway one, qualifies as a real play — a brimmingly warm, entertaining one on a universally relatable topic.
The meticulous and evocative way he expresses himself makes The New One—like a newborn baby—special, unique and lovable.
Birbiglia could have set his loamy, conspiratorial This American Life voice to a traditional stand-up career and been just fine, thank you.
In that moment, we know he’s going to do all right as a father.
I laughed much more than I was even expecting to. I think his storytelling and joke craft are pretty watertight.
No matter how bad your mood, Mike Birbiglia will make you laugh. A lot. Such a lot.
Birbiglia is a masterful humorist with a knack for making the most serious subjects hilarious.
He grabs us at the beginning and holds our attention and good cheer throughout.
Maybe because he’s able to laugh at the situation — and make everyone else laugh, too.

Similarly to his previous work (such as "Sleepwalk With Me") Birbiglia relies upon a well-honed "nice guy" persona. In doing so, he comes off as heartfelt and relatable - not so different from any given audience member who is figuring out life as it goes along.
In this time of political divide and tension, it was refreshing to laugh with an entire theatre of people about the troubles and aches of a universally human conundrum.
But this all serves to make him, well, boring.
The New One works out -- ingeniously.

cn.t: Birbiglia's deeply personal, hilarious show about reluctant fatherhood wins over critics with its relatable humor and emotional honesty, though one dissenter finds it underwhelming. His storytelling charms in an intimate Broadway outing.
